messages:
maria: Heads-up — ACME-prod reporting large p95/p99 generation spikes starting ~03:40 UTC. Appears after the kernel rollout; some requests show auth refresh + KV cache misses stacked. customer-facing errors reported (time outs + 502s).

jake: on it. which region? any reproducible sample?

maria: eu-west-1. Support ticket includes sample trace: lots of wait on storage read + then auth refresh attempt. Ticket id: SUP-8792.

support-bot: @maria SUP-8792 linked to customer ACME (tier: reserved). Notified account team.

sachin: we pushed kernel 5.19.1-rc to eu-west-1 at 03:35 as part of maintenance window. Could be I/O scheduling change interacting with hostfs.

liz: also saw a surge in auth token refreshes around the same time — token TTL expired for a chunk of long-lived sessions. If auth proxy retries are synchronous they can add head-of-line latency.

maria: adding the quick trace snippet from ACME: ```
[2026-03-17T03:41:05Z] request id=abc123 step=kv_get latency=120ms err=cache_miss
[2026-03-17T03:41:05Z] request id=abc123 step=auth_refresh latency=850ms err=502
[2026-03-17T03:41:06Z] request id=abc123 step=generate latency=2300ms
```

jake: that auth_refresh 850ms looks like service-side retries waiting on socket. Can we confirm auth proxy logs?

liz: pulled auth-proxy logs for eu-west-1: several back-to-back upstream connection resets to KMS/auth backend starting 03:36. Not high error rate normally but combined with increased NVME qdepth and new scheduler we get FIFO delays.

sachin: confirmed storage qdepth bumped around rollout due to different I/O classing. We didn't hit limits but tail latency moved from ~10ms to ~200ms for small reads. KV cache cold misses amplify that.

maria: customer impact: p95 from 120ms -> 1.8s and p99 to 2.8s for generation endpoints. They're seeing web timeouts. We should propose an immediate mitigation and a follow-up remediation.

liz: Immediate mitigations (short list):
- 1) Move ACME-prod to a dedicated inference pool (reserved nodes) to avoid noisy neighbor IO.
- 2) Temporarily increase auth token TTL for ACME to cut refresh churn.
- 3) Enable local KV cache warming for that pool (warm on startup, prefetch recent prefixes).
- 4) Roll back kernel scheduler variant on eu-west-1 if traffic doesn't stabilize in 15m.

jake: I can do #1 and #3 now. Sachin, can you patch the kernel rollback playbook? If we rollback, we need coord with infra and oncall.

sachin: I can schedule rollback to start at 03:55 if we decide. Need ack from ops.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-ACME-LATENCY. Pager duty alerted.

maria: I've asked support to apply temporary TTL bump for ACME keys (30m window) — @support-bot can you confirm when done?

support-bot: TTL increased for ACME service tokens to 20m (applied). Monitoring will revert automatically.

liz: after TTL bump we already see fewer auth refresh attempts in last 2 minutes. KV miss rate still high though.

jake: moving the customer now — issuing drain and start on dedicated pool: `infractl pool create --type=dedicated --reason=\"ACME emergency\" --region=eu-west-1` then `infractl move --customer acme --pool dedicated-342`

maria: good. also starting a short-running bg job to pre-warm KV cache for ACME recent prefixes: `python tools/warm_kv.py --customer acme --lookback 1h`

sachin: ops says rollback approved if spikes persist after migration. I'll hold the rollback playbook ready.

liz: quick note for postmortem: interaction vector = (kernel IO scheduling change) + (auth token churn causing synchronous upstream requests) + (cold KV cache misses). We need a durable fix: make auth refresh async/decoupled from generation path and add backpressure protection between auth and I/O.

jake: agree. Action items assigned: Jake (#1,#3), Sachin (rollback playbook + kernel revert runbook), Liz (auth async proposal + instrumentation), Maria (customer comms + postmortem).

maria: update — 03:50 we migrated ACME to dedicated pool and warmed KV; p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 240ms within one minute. p99 still ~600ms due to lingering storage tail. Good improvement.

support-bot: Customer updated: ACME notified of mitigation and monitoring.

liz: leaving a checkpoint: if p99 doesn't return to baseline by 04:10 we execute kernel revert.

sachin: will stand by. preparing revert artifacts now.

maria: thanks team. I'll keep this thread for timeline + postmortem notes. Please add short logs and commands used to the incident ticket.

jake: logging commands + snippets into INC-20260317-ACME-LATENCY.

maria: closing update for now — baseline trending down, customer responded positively. We'll reopen if new regressions appear. :thumbsup:
